summary: 1 finding, fixed: a paired device could keep listing a session as held by a host tab after that tab was gone (F3), because the host's re-announce compares with the snapshot any device's read last recorded and the window tab's session-id change unregistered the file silently. The pool now announces every take and let-go of a session file; heldOnHost and openedBySession converge for 2 devices, 1 window tab, 1 hosted tab, 2 sessions, 3 host changes, any message order (2.9M states, depth 32; 14.8M with a journal event), and each property has mutations that fail it (9 of 9 DETECTED, the bug itself among them).

modeled: LocalHostServices listingChanged/#listing/#listingSnapshot/sessionsChanged/sessions.list; the window tabs' register/unregister/notify; the closed-child record merged by sessionOpeners
the device feed: refresh (one read in flight, one queued), the 350 ms debounce, reconcile/sameRow
abstracted: two devices, one window tab, one hosted tab opened by the window tab, two sessions, at most 3 host changes; a device's two feeds are two devices
only the overlay the property is about (heldOnHost, openedBySession): the index rows are not modeled
out_of_scope: connection loss and reconnect, retain/release of the feed, read errors and backoff
other row fields (status, messageCount, firstMessage, parentSessionPath are not compared by sameRow; not examined)
deleting and renaming sessions, the snapshot cache, several windows of one device
assumptions: A1: replies and events reach a device in any order (the code enforces none)
A2: a handler's mutation and its listingChanged() call run in one synchronous block; a sessions.list reads rows and snapshot in one block
A6: sessionInfoUpdate with a new id is eventually followed by the `session` identity (the code's own comment relies on a hydrate)

findings.title: A device keeps listing a session as held by a host tab after the tab is gone
findings.story: A window on the host holds session s1; the host re-announces a change only when #listing() differs from #listingSnapshot, which every sessions.list from any device overwrites. Device d2 lists the sessions (it sees s1 held). The window's omp reports another sessionId: sidecar-pool.ts's sessionInfoUpdate handler unregisters the file (entry.sessionFile = undefined) and calls no listingChanged(), so windowSessionFiles() no longer holds s1 but nothing was announced. Device d1 reads the list in that gap: the rows say s1 is not held and the host records that listing as its snapshot. The tab then closes: #releaseEntry notifies, listingChanged() finds the listing equal to d1's snapshot and sends nothing. Device d2 keeps the row as held on the host until something else makes it read again (a journal change, a reconnect). The same device with its two feeds (local and global scope) is enough: the snapshot is shared by every read.

changed.inFlight: (d1 :> TRUE @@ d2 :> TRUE) -> (d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> TRUE)
(d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> TRUE) -> (d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> FALSE)

reproduction.test: src/main/remote/host-services.test.ts::LocalHostServices > a device that listed a session as held hears of it when a window's tab lets go of it, even when another device reads the list before the tab closes (with 'control for F3'); src/main/sidecar-pool.test.ts::SidecarPool session ownership (F-OWN) > announces every take and let-go of a session file, a sessionId change's let-go too, and never a repeat

fix.summary: SidecarPool calls onSessionFilesChanged on every actual take and let-go of a session file (#registerSessionFile, #unregisterSessionFile: acquire, the `session` identity, noteSessionFile, the sessionInfoUpdate id change, release), and index.ts wires it to hostServices.listingChanged(). With every change announced when it happens, the one shared snapshot always equals the listing at the last announce or read, so no device's view stays stale (CORRESPONDENCE.md A7); a per-connection snapshot was not needed. listingChanged stays off the per-event path: a repeated get_state report changes nothing and calls nothing. Model: IdChangeAnnounces is gone, IdChange always announces; the bug is the mutation id-change-silent.

NeverHeld and NeverOpener are violated, so a held row and an opener row are reachable
